news.author: Piero Cingari
news.content:
Anyone who has co-signed a loan for a friend knows how the story can end. When the payments stop, the bank calls you.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) has co-signed a lot of loans. It owns a stake in CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV).

It has promised to buy computing capacity the neocloud cannot sell. It also guarantees part of the data center leases signed by its AI cloud partners.

Now credit traders are pricing the phone call.

The cost of protecting against an Nvidia default has more than tripled this year.

Last week, it rose above Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META), one of the chipmaker’s biggest customers, for the first time since at least November 2025, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data shared with Benzinga.

Nvidia’s Credit Risk Now Tops Meta’s

Nvidia’s five-year credit default swap (CDS), the annual cost of insuring its debt against default, stood at 127 basis points on Tuesday, up 226% from 39 at the end of 2025.

On Oct. 21, it edged above Meta’s.

Moreover, it now trades at about twice the CDX North American Investment Grade index and above all six of the largest U.S. banks tracked by S&P Global.

The Co-Signer Is Moving With the Borrower

CoreWeave’s CDS climbed from 589 basis points on July 1 to 967 on July 29. Nvidia’s spread peaked the same day, at 82.

The pattern repeated this month.

Between Oct. 12 and Oct. 22, CoreWeave’s CDS jumped from 903 to a record 1,167 basis points. Nvidia’s rose from 87 to 118, before hitting 130 the next day.

Over the past year, their correlation is 0.80, the tightest among large tech names, ahead of Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL) at 0.69.

Read Also: CoreWeave Debt Fears Hit a Record — Some Are Whispering 'Lehman'

How Nvidia Ended Up Co-Signing the AI Buildout

First, Nvidia is a shareholder.

In January, it bought $2 billion of CoreWeave stock at $87.20 per share, according to a CoreWeave filing.

Second, Nvidia stands behind CoreWeave’s revenue. Under a September 2025 order worth an initial $6.3 billion, it must buy capacity CoreWeave cannot sell to other customers through April 2032.

Third, the guarantees go beyond CoreWeave.

In its latest quarterly report, Nvidia said it “entered into land, power, and shell guarantees for select AI cloud partners’ data center lease obligations in the event of their default.”

Beth Kindig, lead tech analyst at I/O Fund, described the loop in June.

“As Nvidia makes these investments, CoreWeave and Nebius are going right back to Nvidia to purchase large volumes of GPUs,” she said.

As a result, if demand for computing power fades, the bill comes back to Nvidia.

On Tuesday, Nvidia added another signature. It said it will invest $3 billion in Meta’s roughly $37.5 billion equity offering.

The Credit Market Is Picking Sides

Nvidia’s bonds tell the same story. Its 4.95% notes due 2036 now yield about 96 basis points more than the 10-year Treasury, up from about 73 in late September.

Still, the stress is not spreading: the CDX North American High Yield index has barely moved in a month.

Ed Yardeni and Elias Griepentrog of Yardeni Research said in a Monday note that mega-cap tech balance sheets are still treated almost like sovereign borrowers.

For the leveraged builders of AI infrastructure, however, “the credit market is increasingly imposing credit discipline,” they said.

Nvidia sits between the two groups. Its own balance sheet belongs in the first. Its signatures increasingly tie it to the second.

Read Also: Nvidia Is Now Cheaper Than the Average S&P 500 Stock: Wall Street Still Sees Record Profits

At 127 basis points, Nvidia’s CDS is far from distressed levels, and neither Nvidia nor CoreWeave has missed a payment. However, the credit market has started to price the co-signer as if the phone might ring.

Technology giant Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) could report a 15th straight double beat with fiscal first-quarter financials coming Wednesday after hours.

Here’s a look at the earnings estimates, what experts are saying and key items to watch.

Microsoft Q1 Earnings Estimates

Analysts expect Microsoft to report first-quarter revenue of $90.68 billion, up from $77.67 billion in last year’s first quarter, according to data from Benzinga Pro.

The company has beaten analyst revenue estimates in more than 10 straight quarters.

Analysts expect Microsoft to report first-quarter earnings per share of $4.72, up from $4.13 last year.

The company has beaten analyst estimates for earnings per share in more than 10 straight quarters.

Overall, the company has posted 14 straight double beats through the fourth quarter and is going for its 15th straight double beat on Wednesday.

Read Also: Microsoft's AI Data Center Misfire Exposes a Brutal Reality: Billions Can't Buy Time

What Experts Are Saying

With concerns about neocloud financing and capex by big technology companies, Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives sees pressure on the Magnificent Seven stocks like Microsoft ahead of earnings.

“This week will be an important one to gauge the demand trends/GPU building/enterprise capex-driven plans for the Big Tech stalwarts with all the markets watching,” Ives said.

Ives estimates that 800 to 1,000 more data centers will be built in the U.S. over the next few years. The analyst sees hyperscalers such as Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet as winners from this Fourth Industrial Revolution.

Ives highlights $850 billion of hyperscaler AI spend this year against a cloud backlog of more than $2 trillion, meaning capacity and not demand is the constraint.

“Microsoft is the cleanest expression of that setup. Azure moves the stock, but the read that matters is whether capacity is absorbed as fast as it lands, since backlog compounding ahead of revenue is the demand underwriting the capex.”

Ives maintained an Outperform rating on Microsoft stock with a price target of $615.

Freedom Capital Chief Market Strategist Jay Woods highlights Microsoft’s technicals in a weekly newsletter.

"The technical boundaries are quite clear, but quite wide. The $545-$555 area has become a stubborn ceiling, rejecting shares on three separate occasions, while the $340-$350 zone has repeatedly provided a floor," Woods said.

Woods said the stock has failed to break below its moving averages on several occasions.

"Three strikes, and the bulls are back on defense."

The market expert said a failure to break out could see the stock land closer to $460 or fall to the $350 support level.

"Microsoft remains in a longer-term trading range, and until buyers can convincingly clear that ceiling, history suggests chasing rallies near resistance may be a tough trade."

Here are several other recent analyst ratings on Microsoft and their price targets:

  • Oppenheimer: Maintained Outperform rating, raised price target from $570 to $625
  • Truist: Maintained Buy rating, raised price target from $575 to $600
  • Scotiabank: Maintained Sector Outperform rating, raised price target from $615 to $625
  • Guggenheim: Maintained Buy rating, with price target of $586

Key Items to Watch

AI and cloud revenue will be key in Microsoft’s results and management commentary.

The company reported Intelligent Cloud revenue up 32% year-over-year in the fourth quarter, outpacing overall company growth of 18%. Overall cloud revenue was up 27% year-over-year for the company.

Microsoft’s Azure revenue was up 43% year-over-year in the fourth quarter, with the key business surpassing $100 billion in revenue for the fiscal year for the first time.

Investors and analysts will want to see the AI- and cloud-related revenue continue to increase given heavy spending in both areas.

Layoffs could be another key topic of interest with the company pitching employees on voluntary buyouts earlier this week.

As one of the largest companies in the world and a key component of the top U.S. stock market indexes, Microsoft’s earnings and stock reaction could create market volatility. Here’s a look at the company’s weighting in three ETFs that track the top indexes.

  • SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (NYSE:DIA): third-largest holding, 5.97% of assets
  • SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY): third-largest holding, 5.93% of assets
  • Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ): third-largest holding, 6.20% of assets

Microsoft is one of several Magnificent Seven stocks reporting earnings this week, and the company’s guidance and updated AI capex could ultimately overshadow results, but investors and analysts will also be watching the financials.

Microsoft Stock Price Action

Microsoft stock is down 0.3% to $530.95 on Tuesday versus a 52-week trading range of $349.20 to $553.72. Microsoft stock is up 12.3% year-to-date in 2026.

news.author: Jeannine Mancini
news.content:
Roll a ball off the kitchen counter and the family dog will trot around the table to retrieve it. Much of today’s AI, it turns out, would conclude the ball left the universe, a gap Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang has made the centerpiece of his pitch for what comes next.

When the Ball Leaves the Counter

"The next wave requires us to understand things like the laws of physics, friction, inertia, cause and effect," Huang said at the Hill & Valley Forum in Washington in 2025. "The fact that I tip that thing over, it’s going to fall. You know, when I set the bottle down, it’s not going to go through the table."

Those are basics children and pets already have, he said. "And so all of these common sense physical reasoning abilities that children have, that our pets have, most AIs don’t have."

Then came the ball. "You know, I roll a ball over the kitchen counter and it goes off over the top and it disappears. Well, the AI thinks it’s disappeared, but you know, your dog knows it. It’s on the other side."

The dog, Huang said, grasps something machines do not. "It understands this concept called object permanence and it didn’t go into another metaverse. And so it runs around the table and gets it, you know?"

"And a robot needs to learn that if you want to go from this side of the table to that side of the table, you can’t go through the table," he continued. "You’re going to have to reason about how to go around the table."

Put that thinking inside a machine, and it has a name. 

"And so all of these types of physical reasoning things are what’s called physical AI. And when you take that physical AI and then you put it into a physical object called a robot, you get robotics."

That is the pitch for physical AI. Today’s systems excel at perception, generation and reasoning inside digital environments. Physical AI aims at machines that grasp friction, inertia and cause and effect, the know-how robots need to work in factories, warehouses and other real-world settings.

Robots, Factories and a Labor Crunch

"Hopefully, in the next 10 years, this new generation of factories will be highly robotic," he said. "They’ll help us deal with the severe labor shortage around the world."

Nvidia has released foundation models such as GR00T for humanoid robots and has pitched machines as a fix for worker shortages, with Huang using the phrase "AI immigrants" for robots that take on work people are less willing to do.

The gap he is pointing to is simple. Large models trained mainly on text and images are fluent, but they lack a grounded sense of how objects behave. Closing it, Huang argues, is what will move AI off the screen and into the world’s largest industries.

The Dog Still Has the Edge

For now, the scorecard is humbling. The family pet understands that a ball does not vanish when it leaves the counter, and the machines are still catching up. Until robots learn to go around the table instead of through it, the dog keeps the lead.

NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) remains a central name in the AI hardware trade as investors weigh its leadership in data-center computing against an emerging opportunity in humanoid robotics and physical AI.

The stock traded slightly higher Tuesday while the Nasdaq gained 0.66%, the S&P 500 rose 0.24% and the Technology sector advanced 1.03%.

Counterpoint Sees Nvidia Leading Humanoid AI Accelerators

Counterpoint Research expects NVIDIA to remain the leading supplier of AI accelerators for humanoid robots in the near term as demand for physical AI computing expands.

Counterpoint said on Monday that cumulative global humanoid robot AI accelerator shipments could exceed 1 million units by 2030, representing a 144% compound annual growth rate from 2026 through 2030.

The research firm said NVIDIA currently leads the market through its combination of computing hardware, AI models and simulation tools.

NVIDIA also works with robot makers including AGIBOT, Unitree, UBTech, Galbot, Figure AI, Neura Robotics and Noetix Robotics.

Competition Could Increase After 2027

Counterpoint Principal Analyst Soumen Mandal said humanoid computing is beginning to shift from GPU dominance toward a mix of architectures as robot models demand greater performance, lower power consumption and improved thermal efficiency.

Counterpoint expects competition to intensify after 2027, when next-generation AI accelerators begin entering mass production.

Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM) is gaining design wins with a heterogeneous computing approach focused on power efficiency and lower costs, although Counterpoint said its shipment volumes remain significantly below NVIDIA’s.

Custom Chips Could Challenge GPU Dominance

Counterpoint Associate Director Ethan Qi expects GPUs to remain the preferred architecture for running advanced models on devices, but sees custom AI chips gaining ground.

Counterpoint said Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) and Xpeng Inc. (NYSE:XPEV) could expand custom-chip adoption by applying their automotive expertise, proprietary silicon and vertically integrated hardware and software to humanoid robots.

China’s D-Robotics is also building its position through partnerships with Leju Robotics and LIMX Dynamics.

Technical Picture Shows Short-Term Cooling

NVIDIA trades 3.3% below its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) and 2.3% below its 50-day SMA, while remaining 1.2% above its 100-day SMA and 6.4% above its 200-day SMA.

The setup reflects weaker short-term momentum while the stock remains above its longer-term trend measures.

Earnings and Analyst Outlook

NVIDIA’s next earnings report is scheduled for Nov. 18 (estimated).

Analysts expect EPS of $2.48, up from $1.30 a year earlier, and revenue of $109.17 billion, up from $57.01 billion.

The stock carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $342.08. Needham maintains Buy with a $300 forecast, Cantor Fitzgerald maintains Overweight with a $350 forecast, and Rosenblatt maintains Buy with a $390 forecast.

Top ETF Exposure

The Pacer Data and Digital Revolution ETF (NYSE:TRFK), REX AI Equity Premium Income ETF (NASDAQ:AIPI) and First Trust Innovation Leaders ETF (NYSE:ILDR) each hold roughly 10% weights in NVIDIA.

Significant flows into or out of these funds can translate into corresponding trading activity in NVDA shares.

Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026. That’s up from $1.1 billion a year earlier, according to its preliminary IPO filing.

Meanwhile, the company’s long-term infrastructure commitments highlight the growing demand for computing capacity needed to develop and run AI models.

VistaShares CEO Adam Patti sees the filing as “a demand forecast for infrastructure.” Anthropic disclosed major cloud commitments, including:

  • Roughly $111 billion with Alphabet, Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL)
  • $110 billion with Amazon.com, Inc’s (NASDAQ:AMZN) AWS and
  • $31 billion with Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT).

Anthropic’s potential future compute spending could reach hundreds of billions of dollars, although these commitments and estimates should not be treated as spending already incurred.

Read Also: Anthropic IPO Filing Reveals AI Boom’s Next Test: 7 ETFs With Pre-Launch Exposure

2 Ways to Track Listed Semiconductor Companies

  • The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH): The fund holds Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) at approximately 21%, alongside exposure to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM), Broadcom, Inc (NASDAQ:AVGO), Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Micron Technology, Inc (NASDAQ:MU). These companies operate across AI computing, chip manufacturing, networking and memory.
  • iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX): This fund also provides exposure to major semiconductor companies, including Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Broadcom. However, stronger infrastructure spending would not automatically translate into higher returns for either ETF. Chip demand, company valuations, competition and supply constraints will also influence performance.

Patti, whose firm manages the $1 billion VistaShares Artificial Intelligence Supercycle ETF (NYSE:AIS), says capacity, not demand, is becoming the central constraint.

"The constraint is supply, not demand," Patti said. This suggests that the industry’s immediate challenge is securing enough infrastructure to support expanding AI workloads.

“The filing says Anthropic sought more capacity than the hyperscalers could provide and is turning to third-party data centers,” he added. “When the customer is asking for more than the market can build, the build-out has room to run.”

Power Infrastructure Is Another Potential Beneficiary

The First Trust Nasdaq Clean Edge Smart Grid Infrastructure Index Fund (NASDAQ:GRID) provides exposure to companies involved in electrical equipment, grid infrastructure and related services. Its holdings include Eaton Corporation (NYSE:ETN), Quanta Services Inc (NYSE:PWR) and Schneider Electric.

Patti argues that the investment implications extend beyond AI developers to the companies supplying chips, memory, networking equipment, electricity and cooling systems.

"Every dollar committed to cloud capacity flows into chips, memory, networking, power and cooling," Patti said. His assessment highlights how AI infrastructure spending can drive demand across several industries, not just benefit chipmakers.

That creates a potential longer-term opportunity for infrastructure suppliers, though benefits will depend on how quickly planned projects translate into orders and revenue.

Spending Risks Remain

Anthropic’s filing does not guarantee that every announced commitment will become immediate revenue for publicly traded suppliers. Infrastructure projects can be delayed, and AI spending plans and valuations remain vulnerable to changes in demand.

Patti also flagged risks, including customer concentration. “About 20% of revenue comes from two customers, and these figures come from a preliminary filing. The final S-1 and the IPO pricing will be the next checkpoints,” said Patti.

For ETF investors, the filing offers a new lens for examining the AI trade: not just which companies build AI models, but which businesses supply the infrastructure needed to run them.

Investors searching for an artificial intelligence bubble may be looking in the wrong place, technology investor Paul Kedrosky told Benzinga in an exclusive interview.

The number of publicly listed companies has declined, he said, while much of the speculative value has shifted into private markets, where companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI have reached enormous valuations.

Anthropic, which publicly filed its S-1 registration statement Monday, could soon provide a major test of those private-market valuations.

The Private Companies Are the New Public Companies

Kedrosky said investors often challenge his bubble argument by pointing to the relatively modest earnings multiples of publicly traded technology companies.

“Private companies are the new public companies,” said Kedrosky, who co-hosts The Dick & Paul Show.

During the dot-com bubble, speculative valuations were concentrated in publicly traded technology stocks. Today, many of the most highly valued companies remain private for much longer.

Kedrosky estimated that companies potentially coming to market could carry combined valuations of $4 trillion to $6 trillion, roughly comparable in nominal terms to the entire Nasdaq at its dot-com peak.

Anthropic’s IPO Puts Valuations to the Test

Anthropic is planning to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

The company reported $16.3 billion in first-half revenue, up from $1.2 billion a year earlier, alongside a $693 million operating loss.

Reports suggest a potential valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, although Anthropic has yet to set an offering price.

On Polymarket, traders Tuesday assigned roughly 30% odds to Anthropic closing its first trading day worth between $1.75 trillion and $2 trillion, with approximately $2.5 million traded.

The IPO matters to some of Anthropic’s largest backers. Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) has invested at least $13 billion and committed up to another $20 billion, while Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) has pledged up to $40 billion.

Both companies also supply Anthropic with computing power. Anthropic’s S-1 details at least $110 billion in commitments to Amazon and $114.5 billion to Google over the coming decade.

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) has also agreed to invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic. As the leading supplier of AI chips, Nvidia sits at the center of the boom, with its fortunes tied to the industry’s massive infrastructure spending.

Altogether, the agreements detailed in Anthropic’s filing represent more than $500 billion in potential compute spending.

The Race to Cash Out

Kedrosky argues the IPOs are also enormous liquidity events for employees and early investors eager to convert their holdings into cash.

He said he knows of relatively junior Anthropic employees who, after just three years at the company, could walk away with $50 million.

“The race is to the IPO, then to the lockup expiry, and then after that clean up whatever mess remains,” he said.

Kedrosky expects OpenAI to follow Anthropic onto public markets unless the first offering encounters serious problems.

“Unless Anthropic really falls on its face, I don’t see how [OpenAI] doesn’t follow out on its coattails,” he said.

Kedrosky said that Anthropic has roughly a two-week window between the midterm elections and Thanksgiving to complete its listing, and that election disputes could get in the way.

“If it’s prevented from happening, then everything gets repriced and things change radically,” he said.

Beyond the IPOs themselves, Kedrosky warned that a wider repricing of private companies could send shockwaves through financial markets.

“If that gets repriced, it’s the same thing as repricing the Nasdaq at the peak of the dot-com,” he said.

news.author: Piero Cingari
news.content:
Chipmakers powered a broad rebound on Wall Street at midday Tuesday, lifting the Nasdaq 100 1.5% as fresh money for the artificial intelligence buildout pulled tech stocks higher.

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) sparked the move after a $25 billion share sale ended about five times oversubscribed. The suppliers got the reward:

  • Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), which agreed to invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering, rose 1.3%;
  • Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD), which committed $1 billion, rose 5.1%
  • Meta slipped about 1%.

Consumers Are Upbeat, Bonds Hold Steady

The Conference Board’s consumer confidence index jumped to 91.7 in October from 84.2 in September, well above the 81 economists expected, as gasoline prices eased. Durable goods orders rose 1.8% in September, beating the 1.5% forecast.

The 10-year Treasury yield hovered at 4.99%, just below the 5% mark, while the 2-year yield rose 1 basis point to 4.73%. The 30-year yield was flat at 5.31%.

The Federal Reserve’s two-day policy meeting began Tuesday. Chair Kevin Warsh will deliver a decision at a press conference on Wednesday, Oct. 28.

Read Also: Nvidia's Credit Risk Has Tripled This Year — and Just Passed Meta's

Oil Eases

Iranian military officials reportedly met with Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials in Tehran on Monday. West Texas Intermediate crude fell 1.7% to $100.03 a barrel, and Brent dropped 1.1% to $109.48.

Gold rose 0.9% to $4,075 an ounce, and silver edged up 0.4% to $54.55. Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) gained 0.4% to $80,341.

The S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,732, adding 55 points.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.2% to 52,459, as The Boeing Co. (NYSE:BA) dragged. The planemaker now expects to reach a 737 production rate of 47 jets a month in early 2027 rather than this year, and guided to about $3 billion of free cash flow in 2027, well below consensus.

The stock fell 9.9%, on track for its worst session since April 3, 2025, and the slide erased about $14.5 billion of Boeing’s market value by midday.

The Coca-Cola Co. (NYSE:KO) slipped 0.6% despite beating third-quarter estimates and raising its earnings growth outlook.

Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) led with a 3.6% gain, followed by Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL), up 1.7% and 1.5%. The small-cap Russell 2000 advanced 1.1%, and the VIX fell 4.7% to 17.53.

Tuesday’s Performance In Major US Indices

According to the Benzinga Pro platform:

  • The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSE:VOO) rose 0.6%.
  • The SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA) edged up 0.1%.
  • The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) climbed 1.3%.
  • The iShares Russell 2000 ETF (NYSE:IWM) gained 1.1%.

Chipmakers Lead As Refiners Sink With Crude

Technology led the market. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSE:XLK) rose 1.9% as the Meta investments revived the AI hardware trade, and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH) added 2.8%.

Energy lagged. The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSE:XLE) fell 1.9% as crude slipped, while the VanEck Oil Refiners ETF (NYSE:CRAK) lost 2.9% as diesel and gasoline futures dropped about 2% and 1.5%.

Consumer discretionary, materials and industrials also rose between 0.4% and 0.9%, while consumer staples and real estate fell about 0.8% and financials and health care slipped.

Earnings Drive Major Moves

SoFi Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:SOFI) jumped 15.4% after third-quarter adjusted earnings of 18 cents per share topped the 17-cent estimate. The lender raised its 2026 earnings guidance to 61 cents and guided to about 90 cents for 2027, above the 81 cents analysts expected.

Pentair plc (NYSE:PNR) rallied 12.8% after third-quarter sales beat estimates on growth in its water solutions business. The company reaffirmed its full-year adjusted earnings guidance of $4.70 per share and said pool destocking is complete.

AI infrastructure names extended the rebound. Applied Digital Corp. (NASDAQ:APLD) rose 9.4% after closing Monday at its lowest level in a year, and Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd. (NASDAQ:CRDO) gained 9%. Geothermal developer Fervo Energy Co. (NASDAQ:FRVO) added 9.3%, alongside data-center power names.

On the Downside

Xylem Inc. (NYSE:XYL) sank 11.5% after third-quarter revenue of $2.20 billion missed the $2.28 billion estimate. The water technology group cut its 2026 adjusted earnings guidance to $5.40 to $5.45 per share from $5.55 to $5.70.

Armstrong World Industries Inc. (NYSE:AWI) fell 7.7% after adjusted earnings of $2.26 per share missed the $2.39 estimate and the company trimmed its full-year profit outlook on rising costs.

Valero Energy Corp. (NYSE:VLO) dropped 7% with the refiners, as Phillips 66 (NYSE:PSX) and Marathon Petroleum Corp. (NYSE:MPC) each slid about 6%. Euronet Worldwide Inc. (NASDAQ:EEFT) lost 6.4% after cutting its 2026 guidance on weakness in its cross-border payments business.

Looking Ahead

Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) reports after the close, with analysts expecting fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $3.44 per share. F5 Inc. (NASDAQ:FFIV) ($4.26), Waste Management Inc. (NYSE:WM) ($2.18) and CoStar Group Inc. (NASDAQ:CSGP) (34 cents) also report.

Technology giant and Google parent Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG)(NASDAQ:GOOGL) looks to continue a long streak of beating analyst estimates when the company reports third-quarter financial results Wednesday after market close.

Here are the earnings estimates, what experts are saying and key items to watch.

Alphabet Q3 Earnings Estimates

Analysts expect Alphabet to report third-quarter revenue of $128.18 billion, up from $102.35 billion in last year’s third quarter, according to estimates from Benzinga Pro.

The company has beaten analyst revenue estimates in 14 straight quarters.

Analysts expect Alphabet to report third-quarter earnings per share of $3.02, up from $2.87 in last year’s third quarter.

The company has beaten analyst estimates for earnings per share in 14 straight quarters.

Read Also: Michael Burry Eyes the Exit on Walmart, Alphabet and Valero

What Experts Are Saying

It’s been two quarters since Alphabet stock exploded to new highs in May, hitting $408.61. Since then, second-quarter financials and other events haven’t been enough to kickstart another rally.

Shares are down around 21.6% from all-time highs and are up only 1.6% year-to-date in 2026.

After leading the Magnificent Seven in 2025 with a gain of around 66%, Alphabet is the fourth-best of the seven in 2026.

Freedom Capital Markets Chief Market Strategist Jay Woods said Alphabet shares are making a series of lower highs and showing bearish technical signals.

"Unfortunately for the bulls, the technical picture isn’t getting much prettier," Woods said in a weekly newsletter. "With shares now testing the lower boundary of the formation, the $314-$324 zone remains the immediate line in the sand."

Bear Trap

Woods said a key is Alphabet’s strong earnings performance and expectations for AI and Google Cloud growth in 2027 and 2028, which could set up a "bear trap."

"For now, the bears have the technical advantage, but a swift recovery of support could quickly change that narrative."

Needham analyst Laura Martin is bullish on Alphabet ahead of earnings, maintaining a Buy rating and a $450 price target. The analyst sees upside for the company’s YouTube segment.

Martin said YouTube is worth $340 billion and drives upside for Alphabet through revenue growth, advertising and AI tools.

"YouTube’s revs have shifted toward subscriptions, which have higher margins, we believe," Martin said.

The analyst points to YouTube’s increased total TV viewing market share in August and a share that has grown over the last three years.

Other recent analyst ratings on Alphabet stock and their price targets:

  • Citizens: Maintained Market Outperform rating, lowered price target from $515 to $450
  • BMO Capital: Maintained Outperform rating, raised price target from $465 to $480
  • Keybanc: Maintained Overweight rating, lowered price target from $435 to $410
  • JPMorgan: Maintained Overweight rating, raised price target from $420 to $425

Key Items to Watch

Like many of the big technology companies reporting earnings in the coming weeks, attention will be on AI and Cloud for Alphabet, two of the company’s fastest-growing items.

A streak of 14 straight double beats is on the line with analysts expecting revenue and earnings growth.

Alphabet posted year-over-year growth across its four key business segments (Google Search, YouTube Advertising, Google Cloud, Google Advertising) in the second quarter.

The company’s CEO Sundar Pichai said AI investments were paying off across all business segments.

Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year over year in the second quarter.

Analysts and investors will be watching management commentary on Google Cloud, AI, YouTube and more.

A sharp move up or down in Alphabet shares could create volatility in the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and Nasdaq 100, three indexes in which the stock is a key holding. Here are the current weightings in ETFs that track those three indexes, with GOOG and GOOGL included in some.

  • SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average (NYSE:DIA): 11th largest holding, 3.64% of assets
  • SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY): 5th and 7th largest holding, 5.16% combined
  • Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ): 9th and 10th largest holdings, 5.78% combined

Alphabet is one of the most important reports of the week and could set the table for expectations and stock prices of other AI, hyperscaler, cloud and streaming companies.

Alphabet Stock Price Action

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) remains a major AI investment story as the company expands its infrastructure partnerships, scales Muse internationally and works to turn rising AI usage into profitable revenue.

The stock traded nearly 1% lower Tuesday even as the S&P 500 gained 0.5%, and the Nasdaq advanced 0.97%. Communication Services rose 0.1%.

Nvidia Expands AI Partnership With Meta

NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Meta expanded their AI partnership around Meta’s Muse family of models, while NVIDIA plans a $3 billion equity investment tied to Meta’s equity offering.

The companies aim to improve training and inference performance while lowering operating costs.

Their expanded collaboration also includes NVIDIA’s OpenShell Reference Architecture, OpenShell for secure AI-agent deployment and NVIDIA Sentry for monitoring agent behavior.

BNP Paribas Sees $8 Billion Muse Opportunity

BNP Paribas analyst Nick Jones maintained an Outperform rating and a $940 price forecast, implying 49% upside from the Oct. 26 reference price of $630.60.

Jones estimates Meta spends about $180 annually, or roughly $15 per month, to serve the average free-tier Muse user.

He estimates monthly costs of about $90 for Power users and $570 for Maximum-tier users, leaving the product unprofitable at current cost levels.

Cost Reductions Could Drive 2027 Break-Even

Jones said Meta aims to reduce Muse serving costs by 10 times over the next year, which could allow the product to reach gross-profit break-even as early as 2027.

However, he cautioned that users may consume more tokens as they find additional uses for Muse, potentially offsetting some efficiency gains.

Jones believes Meta would need users to complete dozens of transactions annually to break even without substantial cost reductions.

Muse Revenue Could Top $8 Billion By 2028

Jones estimates Muse could generate more than $8 billion in incremental revenue by 2028 with positive gross margins if Meta combines subscriptions with payment transaction fees and advertising.

He said monetization could take longer as Meta experiments with business models and continues prioritizing adoption and engagement.

Jones highlighted Muse’s recent launch in Japan and expects additional international rollouts.

He sees Meta’s large existing distribution base as an advantage in attracting users and testing new monetization approaches.

Technical Analysis

Meta trades 11.4% below its 20-day SMA and 5.8% below its 50-day SMA, reflecting weaker near-term momentum.

The stock also sits 0.6% below its 100-day SMA and 0.8% below its 200-day SMA, leaving it just under its longer-term trend measures.

Top ETF Exposure

The Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF (NYSE:IGPT) holds an 8.32% weight in Meta, while the Natixis Loomis Sayles Focused Growth ETF (NYSE:LSGR) carries a 9.04% weighting.

The VanEck Communication Services TruSector ETF (NASDAQ:TRUC) holds a 9.46% weight in the stock.

Significant inflows or outflows from these funds can translate into corresponding trading activity in META shares.

META Price Action: Meta Platforms shares were down 1.00% at $624.26 at the time of publication on Tuesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) on Tuesday released topline results from its Phase 3 MagnetisMM-32 study evaluating Elrexfio (elranatamab) as a monotherapy.

• Pfizer stock is showing upward bias. What’s next for PFE stock?

The trial studied adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who previously received at least one line of therapy, including an anti-CD38 agent and lenalidomide.

Read Also: Pfizer Expands Breast Cancer Drug Reach with New FDA Nod for Metastatic Disease

Strong Progression-Free Survival Results

The study achieved its primary endpoint of progression-free survival at a pre-specified interim efficacy analysis.

Elrexfio demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction in the risk of disease progression or death compared to three standard-of-care regimens selected by investigators.

More than 75% of patients receiving Elrexfio avoided disease progression or death at the time of analysis, showing an estimated 68% progression-free survival rate at 18 months.

Secondary endpoint data for overall survival remain immature, and researchers will continue monitoring patients until the next scheduled analysis.

Safety Profile and Regulatory Plans

ELREXFIO demonstrated a safety profile consistent with its known characteristics, generating no new safety signals.

Early infection prophylaxis measures helped mitigate infection risks. Grade 3 or higher infections developed in 27.5% of patients receiving Elrexfio versus 18.1% on investigator’s choice, while Grade 5 infections occurred in 0.8% of Elrexfio patients compared to 1.6% in the control group.

FDA Approval for Prostate Cancer Drug

On Monday, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Pfizer’s talazoparib (Talzenna) in combination with enzalutamide for mutated prostate cancer.

The approval covers adults with metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve or -sensitive prostate cancer with homologous recombination repair gene mutations, as detected by an FDA-authorized test.

Election forecaster Nate Silver says next week’s midterms could mark the “end of the Trump era,” as high gasoline prices and opposition to the Iran war add to President Donald Trump’s political troubles.

“If the election goes roughly as the polls say it will go, then in some ways it would mark the end of the Trump era, I think,” Silver said in an interview with Ezra Klein published Tuesday.

Trump would remain president for two more years, but Silver said a poor Republican showing could leave him a “super lame duck,” comparing the potential aftermath to George W. Bush following the 2006 midterms.

Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control of the Senate. Silver’s election model launched in August giving them a 57.3% chance of taking the chamber, and his latest forecast puts them at approximately 76%.

That’s roughly 10 percentage points above the 66% probability assigned by traders on Polymarket, where more than $9.4 million has traded on Senate control.

Iran War and Gas Prices Weigh on Republicans

Klein suggested Democrats might not be Senate favorites if Trump hadn’t gone to war with Iran, driving up gasoline prices.

Silver said Trump’s declining approval rating was “quite correlated” with gas prices, alongside broader economic anxiety.

Regular gasoline averaged $4.27 per gallon Tuesday, compared with $3.05 a year earlier, according to AAA. Silver Bulletin’s polling average shows 55% of Americans oppose the war, against 36% who support it.

Silver estimated that the national political environment has shifted roughly 11 percentage points toward Democrats compared with the 2024 presidential election, exceeding the historical midterm average of 7.5 points against the president’s party.

That has brought states Trump won by double digits, including Texas and Ohio, into contention.

“The fundamental conditions feel terrible for Republicans,” Silver said, also citing strong Democratic candidates and controversies surrounding the administration.

Silver Flags an AI Backlash

Silver identified a potential “AI backlash” as a major election-night storyline, suggesting Republicans could underperform in areas where data centers are being built.

Morgan Stanley has warned AI investors that a Democratic sweep could weigh on infrastructure investment sentiment, potentially affecting companies such as Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA).

Silver questioned whether Republican candidates could attract Trump’s less-engaged supporters when the president himself isn’t running.

“Those people are not gonna crawl over glass to vote for Roger Marshall or Ken Paxton, I don’t think,” he said.

Still, Silver warned that a three- or four-point polling error across several states could erase narrow Democratic leads.

Anthropic has finally shown Wall Street its shopping list, and chip investors liked what they saw.

The Claude maker, which plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, made its IPO prospectus public on Monday. It never puts one price on the computing power the company plans to buy; the space where that total should go is blank. Piece together what Anthropic has disclosed, though, and the bill runs to as much as $567 billion.

A $567 Billion Compute Tab

An earlier draft of Anthropic’s registration statement, now public on the SEC’s EDGAR database, says the company has signed new and amended deals since the start of 2026 carrying roughly $417 billion in future minimum payments, mostly for compute and infrastructure.

The final IPO prospectus adds extra capacity expected between 2028 and 2031, estimated to cost $125 billion to $150 billion outside the main table of commitments.

Add $125 billion to $417 billion and the total reaches $542 billion. At the upper end, it hits $567 billion. That is our calculation, not a total Anthropic published, and it may be conservative.

Read Also: Anthropic Booked $41 Million in 2023 — And $16.3 Billion in the First Half of 2026

Why Chipmakers Are Watching

Compute is the processing power needed to train AI models and run them for customers. Anthropic says it uses four chip types: Amazon.com Inc.’s (NASDAQ:AMZN) Trainium, Alphabet Inc.’s (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) Google’s TPUs, Nvidia Corp.’s (NASDAQ:NVDA) GPUs and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s (NASDAQ:AMD) GPUs. It says frontier models depend on "enormous and increasing quantities of specialized compute."

The commitments point to demand for accelerators and supporting infrastructure, though they do not translate dollar-for-dollar into chip sales for any one supplier.

Anthropic’s compute and infrastructure costs reached $8.9 billion in the first half of 2026, almost four times the $2.3 billion recorded a year earlier, according to the filing.

A Relief Rally for AI Chips

Chip stocks rallied Monday after the filing offered a clearer view of Anthropic’s infrastructure plans. The iShares PHLX SOX Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (NASDAQ:SOXX) rose nearly 3%, while Nvidia gained 2.4%, Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) climbed 3%, Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) advanced 2.3% and AMD added 2.8%.

The bounce came as investors questioned whether the data-center spending boom can be sustained. CNBC described the semiconductor ETF as roughly 25% below its peak, in bear-market territory. The filing offers a demand signal but does not settle whether AI revenue will justify the industry’s infrastructure bill.

For chip investors, Anthropic’s compute needs could support years of infrastructure demand. But commitments are not guaranteed chip revenue — or proof that every dollar invested will earn an adequate return.

news.content:
The most profitable trade in U.S. energy this year just met its first real test. The threat did not come from oil falling. It came from the possibility that a war might end.

Shares of Valero Energy Corp. (NYSE:VLO) fell 8.4% in afternoon trading Tuesday, their steepest decline since early April 2025, when markets were absorbing President Donald Trump‘s “Liberation Day” tariffs.

Marathon Petroleum Corp. (NYSE:MPC) dropped 6.7%, its worst session since April 10, 2025. Phillips 66 (NYSE:PSX) lost 6.5%, the most since Dec. 16.

The VanEck Oil Refiners ETF (NYSE:CRAK) slid 3.3%, cushioned by its international holdings. The fund is still up nearly 65% in 2026, compared with a 12% gain for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY).

Valero Energy daily chart. Source: TradingView

A Margin Repricing, Not an Oil Story

West Texas Intermediate crude fell 1.8% to just under $100 a barrel. Gasoline futures lost 2.2%, and heating oil futures gave up 2.7%.

When refiners fall more than three times harder than the fuels they sell, the market is not repricing the barrel. Instead, it is repricing the crack spread.

The drop also interrupts a rare run. Marathon has risen for 10 straight months, matching the record streak it set between June 2012 and March 2013. October still has three sessions left to decide whether that streak survives.

Read Also: Oil Tops $100 on Iran Fears, Energy ETF XLE Hits New Record: Stock Market Today

Two Signals From Tehran and Moscow

On Tuesday, Iranian state media reported that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei met the country’s top security official after talks in Tehran with Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan.

Khamenei insisted that Iran’s conditions for ending the war must be met. Even so, the four countries agreed to keep talking.

Meanwhile, Russian diesel is moving west again. A tanker carrying 40,000 tons of Russian diesel left Primorsk on Oct. 22 and is due in New York around Nov. 7, Reuters reported last week.

It would be the first U.S. import of a Russian petroleum product since 2022. The cargo is moving under the sanctions relief tied to Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin.

Neither development adds much physical fuel today. Together, however, they attack the premise of the trade.

The Bet Was on Two Closed Chokepoints

Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 11.7 million barrels a day in October, according to Kpler data, up from 9.75 million in September but still about 18% below pre-war levels.

Russia banned diesel exports over the summer after Ukrainian drones damaged its refineries. In the U.S., distillate inventories stood about 9% below their five-year seasonal average in the week ended Oct. 16, Energy Information Administration data showed.

That squeeze pushed diesel margins above $100 a barrel at times. It also lifted U.S. retail diesel to $6.32 a gallon, from $3.63 a year ago.

For Valero, it produced a record quarter. Its third-quarter refining margin nearly tripled to $39.24 per barrel. Net income attributable to shareholders reached $6.8 billion, or $23.89 per share.

A refinery in this environment works like a toll bridge over a flooded river. The toll is worth most when every other crossing is under water.

Talks in Tehran and tankers out of Primorsk do not lower the water today. They do, however, give the flood a timeline.

Read Also: Nasdaq 100 Climbs on Chip Rally, Boeing Sinks 10%: Stock Market Today

Valero Saw the Headlines Coming

On last Thursday’s earnings call, Valero Chief Operating Officer Gary Simmons addressed the pressure directly.

“Some of the downward pressure on cracks is really related to more headlines, [but] when you digest the data and you look at how much volume is actually coming out, and then lifting of sanctions is more just a change in trade flows, I think we will see a recovery in cracks moving forward,” Simmons said.

He added that the Russian deal did not represent a “significant volume.”

Wall Street had flagged the same risks a month earlier. On Sept. 22, Jefferies analyst Lloyd Byrne downgraded both Valero and Marathon to Hold from Buy, with price targets of $401 and $413, respectively.

“The current share price implies 2030 midcycle margins near 2025 levels,” Byrne said in the note.

He named diesel demand destruction, an end to the war and political intervention as the key risks. Five weeks later, two of those three surfaced in the same week.

The Squeeze Has Not Gone Away

The physical market is still tight. Brent trades near $110 a barrel, and the first Russian diesel cargo has not yet reached New York.

Bjarne Schieldrop of SEB said, “There is a significant risk premium in crude oil prices.”

For refiners, the question is not whether that premium exists. It is how long it stays inside fuel margins.

The refining trade of 2026 was never just a bet on oil. It was a bet that two of the world’s most important fuel chokepoints would stay shut at the same time. On Tuesday, investors started to price in what happens when one of them begins to open.

On 8 October 2025, JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM) Chief Executive Jamie Dimon told the BBC he was “far more worried” than others about a serious market correction. He put the odds near 30%.

A year later, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) is up 14%. It also trades at a lower multiple than it did on the day Dimon spoke.

In a less obvious way, part of the correction he predicted has already happened. SPY’s price-to-earnings multiple fell while its price rose. The reason is that earnings grew more than twice as fast as the price.

Price Up, P/E Down

A year ago, the market was expensive. SPY traded at 28.6x the past year’s earnings of its companies. A few weeks earlier, its P/E had hit its highest level in almost a decade.

Then earnings went on a run. Over the past year, the price alone climbed 13%. Over the same period, the earnings of SPY’s companies climbed about a third. That gap did the correcting: the P/E slid to 24.5x.

That still leaves SPY above its median since 2017. It has come down from the top of its range to just above the middle.

Seven Companies, Half The Growth

Split SPY in two, and the picture sharpens. On one side are the Magnificent 7, or Mag 7: Apple Inc. (AAPL), Microsoft Corp. (MSFT), Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Meta Platforms Inc. (META) and Tesla Inc. (TSLA). On the other side are the remaining 493 companies.

The two groups’ share prices moved in step. Both rose between 12% and 13% over the year. Their earnings went separate ways. Mag 7 earnings rose about two-thirds, while the other 493’s rose about a quarter.

That made the seven companies the engine of the year. They delivered about half of SPY’s earnings growth. Their P/E also fell the most, from 39x to 26x.

The Index Tilted Toward Tech

The tilt started long before this year. In October 2017, the Mag 7 produced about an eighth of SPY’s earnings. Today, they produce about a third. Their weight in the fund has followed the earnings up to about the same share.

They are also far better at turning sales into earnings. The Mag 7 keep about 34% of their sales as earnings, compared with about 11% for the other 493. That mix is one reason SPY can trade above its median since 2017: the index now holds a bigger slice of its most profitable businesses.

What Comes Next

Analysts expect the rest of the market to pick up the pace. Their estimates have the other 493 growing earnings faster than the Mag 7 in the fourth quarter. SPY trades at 18.6x the earnings expected over the next 12 months, a multiple that assumes the run continues.

Big Tech’s third-quarter reports continue this week with Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon.

The biggest tech story of the season is still ahead. Anthropic, the maker of Claude and one of the leaders of the AI market, filed for its long-awaited IPO on Monday. Its Nasdaq debut is expected in mid-November. Investors have talked about a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion. If Anthropic raises the $100 billion it is reported to seek, it would be the largest IPO on record.

Anthropic will need time before it can join SPY. The S&P 500 requires a year of trading and positive earnings over the past four quarters. Once Anthropic qualifies, it would be one of the largest additions in the index’s history. It would also tilt SPY further toward tech.

Dimon gave a correction 30% odds. The market took the other 70% and still came out cheaper.

Billionaire Mark Cuban is among the growing number of experts sounding the alarm on an artificial intelligence bubble.

"I’m not a naysayer on AI," Cuban told Steven Bartlett on "The Diary of a CEO" podcast. "I’m the biggest proponent, but you have to be honest about it."

Hyperscalers are taking on so much debt and could soon hit constraints, he argued. He explained that loans for AI companies could get pricier and lead to a doomsday scenario in which companies can’t raise more money.

Still, Cuban praised one of the industry’s most renowned leaders: "I’m a huge fan of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and [CEO] Jensen Huang.” But he said the company is subsidizing the industry.

The former “Shark Tank” investor also named Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) as a company that is borrowing more than it is making.

"It’s a race," he said.

Cuban on the Positives of AI

Cuban also highlighted the technology’s positives during his interview with Bartlet.

"This dwarfs everything in aggregate," Cuban said. "It’s able to make me a lot more productive."

Cuban said AI can make anyone more productive and can also level the playing field in areas like education, where every library, speech, and book can be available to anyone.

"There’s nothing you can’t learn," he added.

When Bartlett asked whether AI is an opportunity or threat, Cuban struck an optimistic tone: "I see it as an opportunity. Wherever there’s change, there’s an opportunity."

Huang Says No Backstop Needed

Cramer’s jab follows Huang’s public defense of the AI cloud provider. Huang said last week CoreWeave doesn’t need a backstop, though some investors argue the chipmaker’s further participation may be necessary if credit conditions continue to worsen.

The bond market has not shared Huang’s confidence. Borrowing costs on CoreWeave’s debt kept rising through the month, with the yield on its 9.75% bonds due in 2031 reaching a record 16.009%. 

CoreWeave has accumulated more than $51 billion in debt and lease obligations to build out its AI infrastructure, and both stock and bond investors are balking at the spending. 

A Wall of Maturities

CoreWeave has about $20.7 billion in debt coming due through 2030 and another $14.9 billion thereafter, with the prospect of higher interest rates on future financing. 

Equity holders have felt the pain too. After going public in March of last year and reaching a peak market cap of about $90 billion three months later, CoreWeave is now valued at roughly $31 billion, per Benzinga Pro data. 

Read Also: Seagate Stock Tumbles Despite Beating Q1 Expectations: Details

Cramer Stays In Huang’s Corner, Mostly

Cramer has spent weeks defending both men. In an Oct. 18 column, he argued Huang has credibility, conceding the public debt market CoreWeave needs to keep growing may be halted, while maintaining Nvidia’s chips hold up. 

He described the bear case as a bet on CoreWeave running out of willing lenders. Cramer pushed back on comparisons between Nvidia and the telecom busts of Lucent and Nortel.

His tone turned more cautious a week later. In an Oct. 25 piece, Cramer wrote CoreWeave’s stock had taken a steep fall with its high-yield debt as the culprit, and noted worries about its ability to service the debt without fresh money from prospective initial public offerings of Anthropic and OpenAI. Both AI labs rank among CoreWeave’s key customers.

Shares showed some life this week. The stock rose Monday, prompting Cramer to ask on X whether it was attempting a rally after a 37% slide over the past month. CoreWeave remains roughly 61% below its 52-week high of $141.79.

Bond yields above 15% sit in distressed territory. If Huang truly believes CoreWeave’s financing picture is improving, Cramer’s dare puts a simple test in front of him.

Nvidia has the cash. Whether it wants more exposure to CoreWeave’s balance sheet is another question.
